problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{csc}⁡x+3=-1-\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{csc}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡x+3 & =-1-\operatorname{csc}⁡x \\ 2\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-4 \\ \operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value: 

$$
x=\text{arcsin}(-\frac{1}{2})=-{30}^{∘}
$$

This value is outside the required domain. To get a value inside the range, we add ${360}^{∘}.$ 

$$
{x}_{1}=x+{360}^{∘}=-{30}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}={330}^{∘}.
$$

So,  our first solution is ${x}_{1}={330}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={30}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={30}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978818/assets/b3c523e882baf0b3a105e10131091e40de686b4c1483f46e7bdc235e30743a6d.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{30}^{∘} \\  & ={210}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x={210}^{∘},{330}^{∘}.$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=210\cdot 330=69\,300.
$$
